utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. And good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, my name is Di Fazio, I appear for the Prosecution together with my colleague, Mr. Doria and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to the Prosecutor's team. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with John Jones I appear on behalf of Naser Oric. With us are Ms. Adisa Mehic, legal assistant and Mr. Geoff Roberts, our CaseMap manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries before we bring in the witness? Yes, usher, please. I'm sorry for this slight delay but it was due to some technical reasons, as I understand it. I don't know exactly what it was but there was a fault with -- I think our monitors or our laptops. I don't know. It has been fixed, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We are going to continue with your cross-examination, which was started by Mr. Jones last Friday and hope to be able to finish today. May I just remind you that you are testifying under oath, pursuant to the solemn declaration that you made last Friday. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Good morning, General Delic.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry I didn't introduce myself on Friday. My name is Mr. Jones, however, when answering my questions, feel free to in fact address the Court and you can even look at Their Honours, if you prefer, rather than necessarily addressing your questions to me -- your answers to me. Now I take it your familiar with the expression which I think exist in your language and perhaps in all languages, "Rome wasn't built in a day"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree that following the aggression of Serbia and Montenegro against the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the RBH government had to build up its armed forces from scratch?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. I believed we started from scratch.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And throughout 1992 it was a situation of chaos as their attempts to defend against the aggression from the JNA-VRS, first through forming TOs and then later through the ABiH; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And would you agree that many fighters for RBH, whom I think you've described in your statement as patriots, did not know much about how units should be formed or who should be responsible for which functions?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. Only the professional personnel in the army and some of the reserve officers had some basic ideas about what a given unit is and how it should be formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And those professional personnel formed a very small percentage, didn't they, of the overall army personnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the full picture, you are completely correct. I just wanted to add that the Bosniaks were far less represented in the overall amount compared to the composition of the population in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And would you agree that many of these issues of organisation were not resolved, if at all, until later in the war, in 1993, 1994, maybe even not even when the war ended in 1995 were these issues fully resolved?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would fully agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to deal firstly with the situation before the ABiH Corps were formed in late 1992 and deal with the TO units, and I'd like you to look at a new exhibit which we'll pass up and the ERN number for the record is 01806867 to 01806869. While that's being passed around, this is a decision on forming Territorial Defence units taken by the president of the RBH Presidency on the 27th of May 1992, and the decision was apparently signed by president Izetbegovic, president of the RBH Presidency. Do you agree firstly that the presidency is the organ authorised to establish TO units?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Presidency was the Supreme Command of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So TO district staffs were not authorised by law to form TO municipal staffs on their own, were they?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct. The newly formed TO Staff formed on the 8th of April or the 8th of April 1992, if I remember it correctly. It had competence over municipal TO staffs, and all formations, all units, that were outside the TO were given a deadline until the 15th of April of 1992, until which time they had to be subordinated under the newly formed TO Staff of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That was the deadline set for the units to be put under the new organisational structure of the new Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its new armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. It was really in terms of the Presidency, though, the RBH Presidency, would you agree that it's necessary firstly to have civilian control over military matters and that therefore the Presidency was the organ authorised to establish TO units and to appoint TO commanders?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I can clarify or I may have misunderstood a part of your question, but the Supreme Command was the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The professional part in charge was the Ministry of Defence, and that was until the 22nd of May when the TO was restructured, the one given the deadline of the 15th of April. And then until then we had the Republican TO Staff headed by Mr. Hasan Efendic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I think we can take this point quite quickly. This decision is to form 39 Territorial Defence units. I think you'll agree that Srebrenica TO is not listed there.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, as far as I can see, that unit is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it would appear from this document that the RBH Presidency at the end of May 1992 took a decision on the formation of TO units but it did not decide to establish one for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, Mr. Jones. I can only comment what I can see here, and as it pertained to my units mentioned here under items 32 and 33. And those are the units that it pertained to. And if a unit does not appear there, one could make the conclusion you made. But apart from that, I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. As far as 32 and 33 are concerned, is that information accurate, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is completely correct. These are the units that existed before that and were later confirmed by the Supreme Command, i.e., the president of the Presidency of the Republic of B and H, the late Mr. Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would ask for an exhibit number, please, for this document. Might be D296 but I could be wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is D296.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, following on from that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Jones. [Microphone not activated] He mentioned 32 and 33. I notice that 30 also refers to the third Tuzla Brigade. Can he tell us anything about it? Would any of these, either under 30 or 32 or 33 have incorporated also Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness didn't receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I think I will have to repeat. I understand that there is some problem with interpretation. If you are not receiving interpretation, tell me straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I notice also in this list that apart from 32 -- under 32 and 33 which deal with Tuzla, 2nd and 1st Tuzla Brigades respectively, number 30 deals also with Tuzla and that's relative to the 3rd Tuzla Brigade. Did any of these three brigades, pertaining to Tuzla, possibly incorporate Srebrenica under them or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I mentioned a while ago, these were the units confirmed by the Presidency, so we took a different order. Instead of issuing an order on formation, when they are being formed which would be logical within the military and civilian system as well as the system of command and control, the Supreme Command instead simply confirmed the situation in the field in this case, in order to reply to your question, not a single unit from Srebrenica was under these formations. These were solely the units falling under the TO Staff in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That was important to make clear. This will become D296, and thank you, General. You may proceed, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And following on from that, we have another document which is similar to the one you just looked at which will be passed up and that ERN for the record is 01812247 to 01812248. This is again a decision on forming Territorial Defence units taken by the RBH Presidency on the 4th of June 1992. Again, I would simply ask you to confirm that there is no Srebrenica TO unit mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, as far as I can see, these are Territorial Defence units from the areas of Sarajevo and Zenica, and a detachment of Territorial Defence in Srebrenik which is a town in Tuzla's environs, to say, 20 to 30 kilometres north from Tuzla, so this is not Srebrenica but rather Srebrenik, a town close to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. So there are no Srebrenica -- there is no Srebrenica TO mentioned in that document, of any description.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no mention of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And just for further clarification, do you agree that before the formation of the 2nd Corps, Srebrenica was not one of the municipalities formed in the Tuzla district?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you also agree that from the start of the war, until at least late 1993, Srebrenica had no physical connection to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so as well, and I mentioned that in my earlier testimony. The distance is about 100 kilometres and it was controlled by the enemy forces between Tuzla and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I again just ask for an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will become Defence Exhibit D297.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, moving now to the formation of corps within the ABiH in late 1992, on Friday you were shown a document, it's P -- it was P279, I don't think you need to see it at the moment. If you recall, it was the decision taken by the Presidency on the 18th of August 1992 regarding the formation of corps. You remember that document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you agreed today and on Friday that the ABiH had to be built from scratch. Would you agree that the establishment of these corps and units in the field wasn't accomplished in one day? In other words, it wasn't completed on the 18th of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, Mr. Jones. In my previous interviews I said, and if I may have the leave of the Chamber, I wanted to say that although everyone realised that we should put the structure in order, but it was a bit of an orphan in the field. It didn't have any influence, it didn't have the financial means, but it solely depended on a commander appointed. Municipalities basically had more power than the corps at the time, and I would dare say it lasted throughout 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you say that situation lasted in 1993 as well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that. As time went by, the situation improved in favour of the corps. It no longer was what it was in 1992, and slowly the relationship between corps and municipal staffs did change, but still it was far worse than 1994 and 1995. Some improvement was made but not to the extent for the corps to be able to function fully as it is required to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So in fact, would you agree that it took months after August 1992 for the corps to function with its zones of responsibility and units as the decision of August 1992 required?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We may have misunderstood each other, Mr. Jones. The corps was not at its full strength even at the end of the war. One can create a team comprising of a group of people but it has to be functional, it has to have de facto and de jure possibility to implement its mission. Many things existed just on paper. But in practice it took a while. If you are trying to make something from scratch, then of course a time has to elapse in order for the institution to stabilise and to implement its mission. To cut it short, I believe the corps was fully structured at the end of 1995, but still it was only to the extent of 70 or 80 per cent of its powers because of the insufficient manning strength, professional experience, problems with logistics, the situation in the field that still existed, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. And in fact as far as the 2nd Corps Command in Tuzla is concerned, you said on Friday that was actually in the vanguard of these developments, in other words it was actually better organised than the rest of the ABiH or large parts of the ABiH, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's entirely so. Unfortunately analysing the documents from other areas, I have to say that despite all weaknesses that we had during the time and in that area that we were much more advanced in relation to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And when I say 2nd Corps command in Tuzla I mean just Tuzla. That excludes Srebrenica. If that's clear, and if you agree.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, yes. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, General, you were also shown Exhibit P129 on Friday and I will be grateful if the witness could be shown that exhibit now. It's dated the 5th of September 1992 so after the decision that we've just seen on establishing the corps. And it's addressed to the Tuzla district Defence Staff. Now, firstly just on that, this is after the decision to form a corps and yet there is still references to district and municipal Defence staffs. That confirms, does it not, what you just told us, that in fact, municipal and district defence staffs continued to exist alongside the corps for some considerable time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In a number of other documents, you will see that the orders were issued but were not implemented for two or three months. The implementation was postponed. For example, when it comes to the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps, the municipality of Srebrenik and Lukavac kept their municipal staffs for another year after they were abolished. So this is something that was specific for that situation and was caused by the circumstances as they existed at the time, and the same goes for this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Now, you see that this document refers in some parts to infantry brigades, for example the 109th Doboj Infantry Brigade as well as infantry brigades in Tuzla, Brcko and other places. I would ask you to look at the part of the document dealing with Srebrenica TO, which is page 4 of the version you have, page 5 of the English. And do you agree that according to this document, there were no brigades to be formed in the Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is stated here clearly, Mr. Jones, under A, that the municipal defence staff and support units were established, that the detachments of the armed forces are established, the 1st and the 2nd detachment and also independent infantry companies. No unit above the level of the detachment is mentioned here, and I have to explain to the Trial Chamber that a detachment is smaller than a battalion and larger than a company, numbering between 250 and 300 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's very helpful. Now I draw your attention to the words which appear in that section, that the war units under A and B are to be set up according to the above organisational order. And so the Municipal Defence Staff is one of those war units. So it's right, isn't it, that this document is ordering the setting up of a Municipal Defence Staff in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be said so. However, in reality, things transpired differently. They were either established or should have been established. This is an order on establishing these units. However, in 1992, as I explained earlier, there were cases where a document simply recognised the existing situation. So there could be two possibilities: Either they were supposed to be established or they had already been established and this order simply recognises the fact. I don't know which case it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You've told us there is a difference, obviously huge difference, in 1992 between the position de jure on paper and the position de facto. And I think what you're saying is you don't know the situation de facto in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely so, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be right then de jure that on paper, this document, as of 5 September 1992, is ordering the setting up of a municipal defence staff in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this document, and bearing in mind that I wasn't present and was not familiar with the situation, I would draw the same conclusion you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And in fact would you agree that given the situation in Srebrenica at the time, Srebrenica being under siege, people starving, et cetera, that this is all highly aspirational in the sense that it's anyone's guess whether a municipal defence staff could be set up in 12 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please that's asking for comment on the situation in Srebrenica. He -- how can this witness know if it was aspirational or not? He emphatically and clearly and repeatedly has said that he did not know the situation that applied in Srebrenica. In order to comment on whether the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a very fair objection considering the testimony of this witness so far on his knowledge on the situation of Srebrenica. I think this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If I may clarify with one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course you can. But please try to avoid -- what has been pointed out to you which is fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You were aware, weren't you, General Delic, in 1992 that Srebrenica was completely cut off from the rest of the world?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And heard stories that there was starvation in Srebrenica throughout 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you heard that it was a chaotic situation in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My question was really in light of those factors, would it be realistic to mobilise a Municipal Defence Staff within 12 hours or is this something of a pipe dream?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again it's a same question being asked. How does this witness know? Whatever the situation that applied in -- it might have been aspirational, it might have been completely pointless and hopeless.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm happy to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters. I'm sorry. I didn't realise it was switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Since it wasn't activated it will all look like it's my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Given those factors which you just mentioned being aware of in Srebrenica, General, do you have any comment with respect to the order to mobilise the Defence Staff within 12 hours? And if not, then feel free to mention -- feel free to say that you have no comment.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My comment would be that the paper will suffer anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not sure that's entirely clear in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you rephrase that sentiment?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. This is an expression that we use in Bosnia, which means that you can put down anything you want on paper. However, whether Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it comes to implementation, this is where the problems arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now sticking with this document a bit longer, please turn to page 2 in both the B/C/S and English and the reference to the Bratunac municipality. My question is simply this: Bratunac had its own Municipal Defence Staff, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, this is what is stated in this document under 3, in Bratunac municipality, that there should be a municipal defence staff together with headquarters support units, meaning that it was the same as in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact the reality is, isn't it, if you're aware, that the Muslims were expelled from the town of Bratunac and the surrounding villages -- firstly, are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that event and I heard about the combat in Kula Grad which presided that and as far as I remember, Bratunac was completely cleansed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And in fact the Defence Staff was set up somewhat in exile, wasn't it, in Konjevic Polje, if you're aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know about the staff being based in Konjevic Polje. I did not know that specific detail but I assumed that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it's correct, any way from this document, at least from what it says, that there was a Bratunac municipal TO, a Srebrenica municipal TO, neither of these comes within the other, does it? These are municipal TOs which are on the same level, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Finished with that document for the moment. I want to go to the position of the military police, first vis-a-vis the TO and then vis-a-vis the corps. And so with the usher's assistance, if the witness could be shown Defence Exhibit D272? Now, this is obviously a substantial document but firstly are you familiar with this order or with this establishment, this provisional establishment?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it specifically but since it involves Municipal Defence Staffs with headquarters support units, this must have reached me as well as the commander of the Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thanks. I'll give you time to go through this document. Just for the record it's dated, and if you can confirm this, it's dated the 25th of September 1992 and it's an order of the RBH Supreme Command Staff regarding, as you said, Municipal Defence Staff with headquarter support units. The document speaks for itself in that regard. So I just ask you: Do you agree that this concerns the temporary formation for Municipal Defence Staffs?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you agree that a temporary formation provides the basis upon which units are brought up to strength and equipped as regulated by the Supreme Command of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, something that is temporary is indeed temporary, which means that it exists until the staffs are finally regulated and until the organisational structure of all municipal staffs in Bosnia-Herzegovina is made equal. That is all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. This establishment is dated 25th September 1992. Are you in fact aware of any other formation which was ordered in 1992, in late 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Jones. I personally think that municipal staffs stopped functioning back in 1992. There were some individual cases where they continued to exist and that was in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps, such as Lukavac and Srebrenik, which lasted one year after they had been abolished. However, in this period of time, the so-called operative groups were established, and also the district staffs started coming under the corps responsibility. On the 29th of September, the command of the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established. Therefore, this is a period of time where the original solutions encompassing municipal staffs were being abolished and they tried implementing new organisational solutions which were supposed to be more favourable for the then-existing organisational structure of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Basing ourselves on this formation document since we don't have another one, I'll ask to you look at page 7 of this document in the B/C/S version, page 10 in the English, where you'll see there is a chart entitled "Municipal Staff Organisation Chart, types 1, 2 and 3." Seven pages in, in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it. The pages are not marked in my document. Or perhaps it's a poor copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think it's the second page if you keep counting, -- in other words if the usher brings it over I can find the page and then direct the witness to it.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the 8th page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the 8th page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Starts with [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, please have a look at that chart and you'll see there is a box for commander, Chief of Staff, assistant for morale, security organ, assistant for logistics, and financial assistant. You see all that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you to go through this chart and this document on the temporary establishment of the municipal defence staff and ask you if you agree that the military police is not mentioned anywhere as part of this establishment.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones, that's precisely so. During my previous testimony, I have stated that from one municipality to the next one, the situation was different. I had a platoon or a company of military police, for example, but that unit is not mentioned in this chart, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But this chart is issued, is it not, by the Supreme Command Chief of Staff in Sarajevo, so this is at least purporting to regular late how municipal defence staffs should operate throughout the territory, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My comment, Mr. Jones, would be the same as in the previous case: Namely that the situation on the ground was different from what was ordered. I, for example, believe that in a town which had 160.000 inhabitants and between 5.000 and 10.000 soldiers, I believe that I needed to have a military police company in that town. Therefore, I chose to continue to have this unit which was later confirmed by the orders that came from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We are going to look now at the position in different districts and municipalities with the aid of P123 so you can put that document to one side and with the usher's assistance, if the witness could be shown P123. And this is a report on established staffs, institutions and units of the armed forces from the RBH Tuzla district defence staff to the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces in Sarajevo. And it's dated 29th of August 1992. So if you look under Tuzla District Defence Staff I think you'll agree that there is a number 5, it's on the first page, a military police company, platoon of military police, and with apparently 208 conscripts, correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what is stated in that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we turn to look at some of the municipal defence staffs, we see that some of them do have military police units. For example, Lukavac municipal defence staff, it's page 3 of the English and I'm not sure what copy the witness has but I did notice that in the B/C/S version. It's page 3 but the heading is a bit unclear.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Well, do you see then that Lukavac Municipal Defence Staff in that defence staff there is a military police company with apparently 78 conscripts?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's in the fourth row. I don't know if it was indeed a company or perhaps a platoon, and it is stated here that this was the military police company with 78 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. That would be below strength if it were actually a company?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we look at Srebrenica Municipal Defence Staff, I think you'll agree that there is no mention of any unit of military police there.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the same is true, is it not, of the Bratunac Municipal Defence Staff which is on the second page in the English, probably the second page in B/C/S as well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask you now to turn to page 4 in the B/C/S, it's towards the bottom, it's page 6 in the English, and it's the units of the Vlasenica Municipal Defence Staff. This is for a slightly different purpose which I'm going to come back to later.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you confirm that Vlasenica is obviously a distinct municipality from Srebrenica and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right. That is an entirely different municipality in a totally different location. The second municipality in the second axis, the population had also been expelled from there. I think that its inhabitants were in Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Its Muslim inhabitants, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Muslim population which was driven out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you could just confirm that we see there that within the Vlasenica Municipal Defence Staff, there is a Vlasenica TO detachment, a Cerska TO detachment, an Djile TO detachment and a Pobrdze TO company, if you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think Cerska might not have been interpreted but you see there is Cerska TO detachment?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, that's under item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. We are going to come back to that later when we look at some other exhibits but I would just ask to you remember that reference to the Cerska TO detachment being under the Vlasenica Municipal Defence Staff. Finally on this document, I draw your attention to the words on the first page, where it says second sentence in the first paragraph, "In connection with item 2 of your order I hereby inform that you we do not have the order to form units for any of the units formed so far from the staff of the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces of the Republic of BH." Now do you agree that this formation from the Tuzla District Defence Staff is still awaiting confirmation therefore from the Supreme Command Staff in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, that follows from my previous answers. The situation in the field was one thing, and paper work and orders is another matter. People try to find the best possible solution. You have to realise that the General Staff was not manned by professionals. In some cases, municipal staffs, in view of their structure, were stronger than a corps. I can tell you that my municipal staff, if it was not actually stronger, was at least equal to the corps staffs. In terms of human resources sometimes we had better resources. I provided food for them. I provided equipment for them. The units I had, I allocated to them so that they could use it. I gave them engineers so that they could establish the Engineering Battalion. In other words, what I'm trying to say, what is stated in documents is one thing and the situation on the ground was quite another matter. There were changes and nobody was held accountable for the fact that the actual situation differed from what was stated. We had situations, for example, where a battalion was ordered to deblock Bosanski Brod which was 200 kilometres away, and the unit which was quite a small unit, had to go through 200 kilometres held by the enemy in order to accomplish that task, which was ridiculous. People who were there on the ground did what they could. Mr. Halilovic, who was only a few years older than me, and I, were not up to the task. We were quite young at the time. I was 35 years old. When you take into account all of my experience and all of my schooling, I had perhaps 22 years of experience and eight years of schooling. However, that wasn't enough in order for me to properly face the tasks as they existed on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that answer, General, and in fact that was precisely what I was getting at. And to be absolutely clear, there is no criticism whatsoever that the forces were improvising, struggling in a desperate situation to put together a resistance. It's simply to establish that that was the situation. So I hope that's clear. In fact just finally on that subject, paragraph 2 of this document, on the first page, says the "reforming that is already started was temporarily stopped because of intensified combat operation in our area." So that in fact confirms, does it not, that combat operations, not to mention all sorts of other problems meant that many units were not being properly formed in Tuzla district right through 1992, if you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with the usher's assistance if the witness could now be shown Defence Exhibit D273? And while that's being passed up, it's a document of the RBH Defence Ministry, Sarajevo Territorial Defence Staff, signed by the then-commander of the Territorial Defence staff, Colonel Hasan Efendic on the 17th of May 1992. If you see the title order on organisation of military police units, the introduction, I'll just read it for the record, "In order to more effectively and rationally carry out tasks within the competence of the military police of the RBHTO and regional TO staffs, I hereby order," and then, "1, organise TO military police units at the level of the RBHTO staff and regional TO staffs." Now I draw your attention to paragraphs 3 and 4. Paragraph 3 organises, does it not, or provides for the organisation, of MP, military police units, at the level of regional TO staffs, regional staffs; is that correct? With the exception of the Sarajevo District Territorial Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones. That is precisely what item 3 states.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then paragraph 4 orders that all TO military police units not organised in keeping with items 1, 2 and 3 or paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of this order should be disbanded? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not clear to me, Mr. Jones, either that or the translation was not correct. In view of the fact of what I said just a while ago, could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's actually paragraph 4 rather than paragraph 3. I think that might have been the mistranslation and in English we have "disband all other TO military police units," which I think is [B/C/S spoken] in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely so. And item 4, not 3, it is regulated that all military police units formed at the level of municipal staffs to be disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So in other words, and it's clearly set out, isn't it, in paragraph 4, that military police units should not be formed at the level of municipalities, according to this order?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another of the absurd situations that took place, to abolish something that was formed in one place and wasn't in another, as if we had formed armed forces and the single centre to regulate it all. But the situation in the field was quite the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But as far as this order is concerned, whether it's absurd or not, it would mean that Srebrenica, being a municipality, was forbidden to have a military police unit?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the order, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 9, it says that only officers of the military police shall have the right to exercise the legally envisaged powers of the military police. So that would mean, would it not, that at the municipal level these powers of the military police could not be lawfully exercised?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, it states the following here: "The authorities given to the military police by law can implement only the officers of the military police." And there is an addition, "Irrespective of the particular military police unit, as well as the composition of platoons or squads who -- that deal with the issues of forensics and investigations as well as on site investigations."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would Your Honours give me one moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to move to a different document which is P143, which again this is a document, General, which you were shown on Friday. And again, for the sake of the record, this is a document of the Tuzla district Territorial Defence staff dated 14 October 1992, and signed by the commander, Zeljko Knez. You spoke about this document on Friday so I won't ask about it in any detail. Firstly, however t would help if you would clarify one matter. In paragraphs 5, 7 and 8, we see OKSO. Can you confirm that stands for [B/C/S spoken], in other words district defence staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, looking at paragraph 1 of this order, it refers to setting up military police units in municipal defence staffs, including Srebrenica, but elsewhere as part of -- parts of brigades. My question is: Isn't the right why exceptions are being made for those municipalities firstly for Bratunac and Vlasenica, that as you said the Muslim population had been expelled and that's why the MP units were not to be formed in brigades?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the intention of Mr. Zeljko Knez, who was the commander, was, what was it that he was trying to achieve in the field but I can make the assumption that you made.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Srebrenica, would you assume, then, is an exception because, as you've explained, it was cut off from Tuzla and under siege?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, if you are seeking to get a comment on my part about Srebrenica, it would be the following. Mr. Zeljko Knez, who was then the commander of the regional staff and later the corps commander, knew about the situation only to the extent of the information he received through ham radio operators and through some other channels. He tried to work on the situation but whether any of that was actually implemented, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Really just to clarify this for us, if you can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, excuse me, just a correction for the transcript. The witness stated that Mr. Knez was trying to exert some influence on the situation via documents but whether any of that was received or not, and not implemented as it was interpreted, actually what he was trying to say is whether any of it reached Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. General, you heard Madam Vidovic. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was a good correction, and whether any of the orders reached Srebrenica, I don't know. That's what I already stated before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, if you could clarify this for us, then? Is it right that in those municipalities which are mentioned in paragraph 1, Zivinice, Banovici, Kalesija, Zvornik, Celic, Vlasenica, Srebrenica, Bratunac, and Olovo, they had no established brigades and that's why the commander of the district Territorial Defence -- Territorial District Defence Staff was ordering military police units to be set up and attached to the municipal defence staffs.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you, Mr. Jones. This is not about brigades but, rather, about brigades as well as municipal staffs, so both. And even we have the specified staffs. Tuzla was not mentioned here, for example, but I did have military police. So I would add to your comment that it included municipal staffs as well. Not only brigades. The units were not formed and hence, Mr. Knez ordered that they be formed. It is possible that none of it existed, neither within the brigade, nor within the municipal staff, and then we have them mentioned here, Zivinice, Banovici, Kalesija, Zvornik, Celic, Vlasenica, Srebrenica, Bratunac and Olovo. We said that Vlasenica and Tuzla did --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters's correction, "Lukavac and Tuzla."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- did have those units so again we have the confirmation of the situation in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I won't stay with this much longer but I think we need to be clear I'll just read the first sentence of the order. "One, form military police units up to the level of a company of 105 conscripts in the municipal defence staffs," and then those places are listed and I won't read them again, "and as part of the brigades in the remaining municipalities," end quote. So my point was this. For those places which are listed, we are talking about military police units being formed in municipal defence staffs and then for the remaining municipalities, we are talking about forming military police units as part of brigades. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now if we go to paragraph 2, or item 2 of this order, it says that the work of the military police units would be controlled by the chiefs of security in the municipal -- municipal defence staff, correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is incomplete, Mr. Jones. As far as I can see here, [B/C/S spoken], interpretation would be chiefs of security in municipal defence staffs and/or brigades shall control the units of military police in professional terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is my microphone working. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think we can leave brigades to one side because we are just talking about the situation in Srebrenica now so leaving brigades to one side, I want to remain on this theme for a moment. Isn't it then correct to say that the work of these security chiefs on the municipal level, their work is to be controlled by the chief of security of the Tuzla district staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is literally translated is what it roughly states in -- stated in the document but there are two types of command and control. One is horizontal, team communicates with a team, and then vertically, we have relationships between unit commands. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I want to come to that in a moment. I first want to establish just what it is actually stated in this order and it's right, isn't it, that in paragraph 2 of this order, there is no mention there of any role of the commander of the municipal defence staff in controlling the work of the chiefs of security in municipal defence staffs?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And indeed if one looks at paragraph 5 now, this is why I asked you to clarify earlier what OKSO meant, doesn't paragraph 5 provide that the district organs shall regulate the tasks of the military police in their powers in a special book of instructions, firstly?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, it states here that the security organ of the district defence staff will perform that function.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. And then in paragraph 7, that sets up a reporting obligation according to which the military police in municipalities have to report to the military police in the district staff. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. This is the horizontal link.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm puzzled why you describe that as a horizontal link. Surely a security chief on a municipal level when he reports to a security chief on the district level is reporting vertically.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From your standpoint, that is so. But I have to reiterate, there are two types of relationships. As a municipal staff commander, I had my immediate communication with the commander of the district defence staff, and on a daily basis I sent my reports. And this pertains only to a part of the reports in connection with the activities of the military police, not the complete set. I had a combat report to issue, reflecting the last 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I may come back to that but again still sticking with just what this document states, paragraph 7 does not state any reporting obligation of military police on the municipal level to the commander of the municipal defence staff, does it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And before I forget, but on a slightly different matter, would you agree that while there is a stamp here of the Kladanj Municipal Defence Staff or Municipal Assembly, Territorial defence Staff, there is nothing on the document that you have to indicate that it was ever received in Srebrenica? There is no stamp that it was received in Srebrenica; that's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is yet another document which is not set up correctly in its last page. It should have stated "to be distributed to," and then the addressees plus the archives. This document should not reflect the situation as it does, whether something has been delivered to someone or not. I only confirm that I recognise the signature of Commander Zeljko Knez and that I received it and that I worked on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I was just asking about the stamps, though, on the first page. Those stamps from the operations group in Kladanj and the Territorial Defence staff in Kladanj, indicates that the document was received in Kladanj, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a stamp with the word "Kladanj." The stamp I have is the stamp of the Tuzla District Staff of the TO. This is what it states within the stamp itself. The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, District Staff Tuzla, and then in smaller letters, Territorial Defence, and we have our coat of arms. So I don't have the copy that you have, apparently, and there is no mention of Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put the first page of the B/C/S version on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know what the witness is looking at, Mr. Jones, so I want to make sure first and foremost.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, do you see on the right-hand side, General, the two stamps [B/C/S spoken] and then Kladanj at the very bottom of one stamp and then [B/C/S spoken] Kladanj, and then Kladanj again written at the bottom, on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was looking at the wrong page prior. I was looking at the last page instead of the first one. I see the stamp here. These are probably stamps from registry books of the municipal assembly of Kladanj, as well as the operations group, and the dates are the 23rd of October and the 27th of October, but could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact just one question for our benefit, really. Kladanj is a very long way to Srebrenica -- from Srebrenica, isn't it? There was no physical connection between those two places at the time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The closest free territory to the municipality of Srebrenica was Kladanj but that's 100 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Now, just a question on the military security service, the SVB. Isn't it right that within the SVB, there is a special system of subordination which is distinct from the other organs and chains of command within the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And that's what you've been describing as a horizontal relationship; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you still describe it as horizontal when we consider in a corps structure, when you have an assistant commander for security in a corps, would you not regard him as a superior to a security officer in a brigade? And further on down to battalions and companies?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way, horizontally speaking, yes. Horizontally, I reiterate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree that as far as the military security service is concerned, that only the high level commands at the level of the corps commander or higher, had full access to the methods and knowledge of the functioning of the military security organs?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, a unit commander that has a military police organ should be informed, but I do agree with you that they should have the full picture and information as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But would you agree that, let's say, a battalion commander or a company commander may well not in practice be informed by the military police, that they would rather report up the SVB chain to the security chiefs in the corps or brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, I don't understand the question fully. Are we talking about a military police platoon commander or a battalion commander or a corps commander in general? If we are talking about command responsibilities in general, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I was talking about the SVB reporting chain and that at the lower level, battalion commanders or lower level units commanders, that they would not necessarily be informed by the SVB organs within their unit of their work?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reply would be yes, but with your leave, Your Honour, I could explain the functioning of that organ of military security.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My one hesitation, Your Honour, is I'm somewhat short of time in fact as we are going along today. So, Witness, if you could save that answer we may come back to it but I want to move to a new area, given the shortness of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we have the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this would be a suitable time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Jones, and General Delic, please try to keep your answers as concise as possible because we are running short of time and would like to finish your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In fact this next series of questions will mostly require a yes or no answer but, of course, don't hesitate if you need to elaborate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, General, I want to ask you now about the draft combat action sheets which you were shown on Friday and I first have some general questions about the project and I do want to make clear before I start again that there is no criticism if the project wasn't completed or anything of that nature but I need to establish precisely what was done and what wasn't. Now, on Friday you said of these sheets, you said, "This is raw material, it had not been analysed, it was being sent to experts for analysis." Now, would you accept that these combat sheets were drafts, essentially?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've said earlier, this was raw material for the project organised by the General Staff of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting at all but I think that there is a clarification that should be made or we should accept. Mr. Jones used the expression drafts. We have evidence that these documents have been signed off by this witness and other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They are no longer drafts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If they are no longer drafts as I understand that word and if Mr. Jones wants to use that word then we should be absolutely clear from the witness that they are, in the classic sense, a draft, a document prepared before its final state, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's a very valid -- in fact I was going to stop Mr. Jones initially when he referred to the documents as draft combat reports. But you followed the discussion. Once you signed these documents, at least one of them, because the other two that we had seen were signed by different persons, would you still consider them as drafts or did they become a final document for whatever it was worth? And for whatever purpose it was meant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was indeed initial work material. If you want my opinion, it reflects the events and perhaps the participants of the events, number of people and the result of the operation was something that was to be done by a team at the level of the General Staff or, rather, the joint command of the then Federation army. So they were supposed to finalise this and translate that into final form. Last time, when I testified, I said that we attempted to ensure that the form was filled in, in a uniform manner for all operations. That's why we created teams that were supposed to review this. You know that after the war everybody considers themselves to be victors and we were worried that people would amplify and boost the results of the events. What we know for sure is that the events did happen. We know the losses at the level of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, we don't know what happened on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are taking too long on this. So basically let me put it to this -- like this: Once you signed that document yourself, I'm referring to the one which you signed, that -- from that moment onward, no one would redraft that document, but they would process that document together with other similar ones for whatever purpose they were meant, but as far as you were concerned, that document was finalised when you affixed your signature to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the fact that it was signed and that it was there on paper does not mean that it was anything but initial material recording the event. The analysis was supposed to be done by a professional team, including both soldiers and civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think that's clear enough, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I do need to pursue this a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As much as you like. Trying to make your life easier, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that and it may be semantics whether we call it a draft or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What I want to establish and if you could answer with yes or no we could get there. You said these sheets were to be sent for final analysis. That final analysis was not carried out, was it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you know?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, it was not. At the time I was corps commander, I remained in that post until the 1st of October of 2000 and the project was not completed until that time. It started in 1997 and it went on for three years while I was the commander and it was never completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So these sheets were not finalised were they, and again, a yes or no, if you can. They were not finalised. JUDGE AGIUS: It's not these sheets because it's -- the exercise for which they were meant was never completed?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's what I'm seeking to establish, Your Honour, how to refer to these I'm referring to the actual, physical sheets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But those -- you shouldn't put it to him that those sheets were not finalised. Those sheets were finalised. It's the analysis that would have followed those sheets which was never completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's precisely it, Your Honour. Let me approach it a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The information contained in these sheets in these documents, was not verified in a final way, was it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reply will perhaps be unclear. It was verified by those people who drafted that, who signed it but not verified by the people to whom it was intended and who were supposed to use it as material for final analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And these were not published, this project did not result in the publication of these documents, did it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that you cannot personally vouch for the truthfulness of what is contained in these -- in these documents?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely so. I told you last time that a group of senior officers who were from Srebrenica and the surrounding area definitely participated in recording the events. However, there was a group of officers outside of that area who were from Tuzla and that area who were also involved in the project and they wrote into the forms what they were able to hear and what they learned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. In light of that do you accept that the information contained in these - I'll call them sheets, just for convenience - contained in these sheets which is inaccurate, not necessarily deliberately so, but because it has not been checked and finally verified? Is that something you'd accept?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, I agree with your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've told us on Friday and again today that one of the reasons for this project is that there might be exaggeration and to show documents in a different light, you said. Now, when you spoke of the risk of exaggeration, did you consider it being part of that risk that commanders in some areas would be credited with the role in actions in which they were not involved?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subconsciously, yes, you're entirely right. That was precisely our concern. After the war, everybody likes to declare themselves heroes. Everybody wants to portray themselves in better light than it actually was in reality. Everybody wanted to record forever their roles in certain historical events, and we all knew that it was very important for posterity to ensure that these events were analysed properly. This is why we attempted to control that process by using reviewers, including both professional soldiers and civilian experts. As far as I know, over 20 Ph.D. holders were the University of Sarajevo were involved in the project, and they were supposed to give an objective quality to it to be used in future by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you recognise that risk as relating also to commander Naser Oric? That he would be attributed roles in actions in which he had perhaps not been involved?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never gave that a thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Just before we look at some of these drafts do you know that the following people were in charge of this project, firstly, Rasim Dupljak?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, in the joint command, there were dozens of people, not just Rasim Dupljak who were tasked with that. As far as I know, there were at least five to ten teams of people from various fields, such as logistics, command and control, mobilisation, combat operations and so on. I personally know Rasim Dupljak and know that he was involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then for two other names, again you can just say yes or no whether they were involved, Muhamed Sestanovic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that person, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Then Salih Jaliman?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of him but had not contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you hear of him being involved in this project?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard that he was a member of one of the teams but I didn't know that that was indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to start by asking if the witness could be shown D156. It's a Defence Exhibit, and this is not one of the sheets you were shown. It was P86 at one stage but it was withdrawn as an exhibit by the OTP. Now, if you could firstly have a look at this sheet and I'd ask if you agree that it's in the same format as the other three sheets that you were shown last Friday.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, these are the same issues and same format.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you turn to the last page, you see that it appears that one of the reviewers was a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can't follow because we don't seem to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's D156.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we could put it -- is it on the ELMO? Okay. It's on the ELMO now. Thank you, thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you agree that on the last page, it appears that one of the reviewers was a Ramo Hodzic, not sure if that's come out correctly in the English, but in the Bosnian it should be Ramo Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that. He's a senior Lieutenant or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you agree that it looks like one hand has signed or has written in all the names? Is that something you would agree with, firstly?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the entire document was written by one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Shouldn't these forms in fact be filled in, at least signed by different people in order to ensure that the information was carefully checked by more than one person?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. However, if these people are indeed behind it, then their names could have been written in. This information was probably used by the team so that the team could later on, when analysing this information, call back the people compiling the document in order to establish the relevant truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree that there is a purported signature there by Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, Mr. Jones, just the name of Zulfo Tursunovic. I don't know what his signature looks like but I assume that this entire document was written by one hand and that this is not his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well as far as Zulfo Tursunovic is concerned, you've mentioned him before, are you aware that he's in fact illiterate?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is right, that he is illiterate but I'm not sure about that so perhaps I should rephrase my answer and say I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. I would ask if the Court would now refer to D157?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That's a statement, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's a statement by Ramo Hodzic given by the investigators of the OTP of this Tribunal. I'm afraid since we don't -- I don't think we have a version in B/C/S, so I'm just going to read a part of the statement. It's paragraph 18. And in that statement, Ramo Hodzic says of this document, the one we've just seen, the original of which had the ERN number 02621257, to 02621260, "I've never seen this document previously. I was never involved in the preparation of this document. I was never involved in the preparation of the -- any other documents like this one. In fact I've never been part of the 28th division." Now, you've told us how these were not final products. It's not a criticism, but would it surprise to you learn that people's names had been added as reviewers who were in fact no such thing?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not how it should be but when it comes to Srebrenica, nothing would surprise me. As I've told you before, this project was conducted by a group among whom there were members who were not in Srebrenica, because that group was disbanded, people were demobilised, including many of those who were there originally, and as far as I know, this project went on between 1997 and 2000, or maybe even later, which means that it took place many years after the events in Srebrenica. So it is possible that somebody was included here in the belief that that person was a participant in the events and then that was done in order to be able to call that person later on to clarify things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So the fact that a person's name is listed as a reviewer doesn't mean that he had in fact been consulted at that stage as a reviewer?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's obviously the case, based on this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: A bit more about this document. This refers to an action which allegedly took place on the 10th of June 1992. It too says that the units involved in the combat action were part of the municipal -- Srebrenica Municipal Defence Staff, Territorial Defence Staff. That's on the 10th of June 1992. Now, we've seen with P129 and you've agreed that there was no Srebrenica Municipal Staff on paper, at least, until considerably after June of 1992. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's possible that that's how it was. One of the reasons, potential reasons, was that the later -- that the unit later did become part of the municipal staff and that was the reason why it was treated that way. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Although the form itself says that that was the -- the unit was in that formation at the time of the execution of the combat operation. So that could be inaccurate information, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. The unit was indeed perhaps later within the municipal staff and perhaps that was the reason why when the document was drafted it was listed as such. What actually happened is that the documents that came later actually recognised the situation that had existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just on the same theme, according to P76, which you were shown on Friday, Naser Oric was formally appointed as commander of the Srebrenica TO on the 27th of June 1992. So it would also be inaccurate, wouldn't it, to say that he was the commander of the Srebrenica Municipal TO as of the 10th of June?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but what the witness said is quite the opposite of what is stated in the transcript. What is stated here is that the document later recognised the situation that existed. What the witness said in fact was quite the opposite, that at the time the situation was different than what it was when the document was written. So could the witness please repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that and I will repeat it. I wanted to say that at the time when this was drafted, and this is a uniform form which has certain information that is needed, and it couldn't be avoided. So it is possible that that unit at the time was not a part of that municipal staff. However, at the time when this information was entered, and later on, if the unit was indeed at that point within that municipal TO staff, then that's what was entered into the form. So the actual situation at the time when the combat was conducted was not the same as at the time when this document was drafted. Perhaps that units was originally an independent one but later on it became a part of that municipal staff and this is why this document reflects that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, and a final clarification on that. When you say perhaps that unit was originally an independent one but later it became part of the municipal staff do you agree that that -- first, the fact that the unit was possibly at the time of the combat operation an independent one but it later became part of the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely so, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if we could -- if the witness could please be shown P87 which you were shown Friday, related to Ducice. Now, this concerns an alleged action in Ducice village which began and ended according to this form on the 19th of June 1992. I think you'll see that at paragraph 1 and paragraph 12. And the unit which carried out the action according to this was the Osmace TO and the operation was planned by Mirsad Dudic. It's right, isn't it, that this form does not say that Naser Oric planned the attack?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, I've stated that this was a unique kind of an event, namely the unit conducting combat here, actually the units are two TO staffs, TO Staff Osmace and TO Staff Srebrenica. The commander, Atif Krdzic, was undoubtedly the one conducting operations. Naser Oric is not the commander here. He's mentioned under item 4.
