You have been shown a Defence Exhibit 296 and -- where you had "some Territorial Defence units shall be formed and you may remember that Srebrenica was not among them." Now, does this mean that you had soldiers, say, TO-free areas within Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's definitely the case. There were much such areas, such as Bijeljina, Banja Luka, Doboj, and so on. Everything that was occupied by the former JNA, even before the aggression, or perhaps locations where the Serbs had a majority in Bosnia-Herzegovina, they did that together with the JNA. However, there were also certain municipalities in exile. For example, from Zvornik, people came to Tuzla, from Srebrenica and some other places, people came to Tuzla, and established their own civilian authorities which tried to establish military units that would enable them to go back to their areas. In this order on the establishment of corps, you will see that it says the establishment of the Banja Luka Corps and Banja Luka is some 300 kilometres from Zenica, if not more. So the plan was to organise the refugees into units and to send them to liberate their areas. This is how it was conceived. However, it was not always practically implemented in this way. So it is possible that in some places there was no Territorial Defence. Then there was another order dated the 8th of April 1992, ordering all units to be united into Territorial Defence, meaning the Green Berets, the Patriotic League and so on. All of them were supposed to unite in a part of armed forces which would be known as the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, this is something that was not implemented in all areas. The same goes for the abolishment of municipal staffs in some places, they were, and in some places they weren't. There were certain areas where there were great conflicts in the staff itself. In Lukavica, for example, there was just one brigade and the Territorial Defence staff, and the brigade was resubordinated to the TO staff which created major problems within the command and control system. Later on, the situation changed and it was vice versa. And that again created animosity between these two commands. The situation on the ground was followed. On Friday, as I told you, it was on some occasions simply verified or recognised. In some instances they recognised the shortcomings, the mistakes, and adopted solutions which later on proved to be quite positive. This is why the military police platoons and companies were established. I would have to add the following. When it comes to horizontal links, the idea was to take as much power as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have an additional question. Almost at the same time when we had this order by the Republic of Bosnia for the Presidency, almost in the same time in 27th of June, Exhibit P76, you have been shown from the Territorial Defence Staff of Sarajevo that Naser Oric was appointed commander of the Srebrenica Municipality TO, Territorial Defence. Now, am I correct in assuming that this Territorial Defence was something different from what you had described before? Or was it the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's been described as almost the same time. We are speaking about a month later and I think we are all aware of the evidence that the Serbs occupied Srebrenica until May 1992 and so I think this -- the witness is going to be misled if there is a suggestion that -- I'm not sure what Your Honour's suggestion is, but there is a month later, this other document, and if an open question can be put to him, then that's fine. But we wouldn't want any suggestions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: My question is very simple. I just wanted to know what Territorial Defence meant. I mean, we have a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: This document of the 27th of June 1992, Naser Oric was appointed commander of the Srebrenica Municipality TO/Territorial Defence Staff. Now, my question is: What is meant by the term Territorial Defence staff? Is it different from what you had described before or is it almost the same or what else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just try to answer it as briefly as possible, please, general, because we have already overstayed and this courtroom needs to be made ready for 2.15, and they need half an hour for that.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the TO staff is a military term for command and control of the TO units in the territorial structure at the level of the municipality. However, in 1992, not a single municipality had identical conditions to another one. Not only in Srebrenica but elsewhere in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The municipalities neighbouring Tuzla had a situation that was radically different from the one existing in Tuzla, both in terms of human resources and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: May I conclude from this that the municipalities may have had their own sort of Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct. In principle each municipality had their own TO staff, any larger municipality, and I believe in Bosnia-Herzegovina that was any and every municipality, and it comprised units, level of brigade or lower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the end of your testimony, General. We managed to finish today, with just under ten minutes over the time allocated. On behalf of Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser on also on my own behalf I should like to thank you for having come over to give testimony in this case. You will receive all the assistance you require now to facilitate your return back home at the earliest and on behalf of everyone present here I wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow we start at 9.00, I think in this same courtroom. You have that witness. How long -- who is going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't have the honour of taking that particular witness, if Your Honours please. But I gather that he won't be long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I gather it will be -- one hour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One hour on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: One hour, possibly less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: be reconvened on Tuesday, the 31st day of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
